title: Scalable tone ramp and tooltip pattern for variance & rollout views
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a scalable tonal ramp and compact tooltip interaction pattern for the Console's variance and rollout dashboards. Objective: create a consistent visual language for small-metric sparklines, cost-variance heat indicators, and rollout state tooltips that scales across density (compact / default / expanded) and theme (light / dark / high-contrast). Deliverables: Figma component library updates, token recommendations (color ramps + elevation + spacing), a clickable prototype demonstrating hover and keyboard tooltip flows, and an implementation handoff with usage examples for the metrics and rollout teams. Constraints: must respect existing color token accessibility targets (WCAG AA for normal text, 3:1 for UI indicators where possible), be feasible with existing CSS-in-JS token pipeline, and keep DOM footprint minimal to avoid telemetry and render cost spikes on heavy dashboards.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: aligned with PM (Nora Li) and ENG (Diego Ramos). Agreed scope to target three surfaces: cost variance sparkline, rollout state chips, and per-route latency microcards.

2026-03-04 — Exploration: generated three distinct tone ramp systems (directional, centered, and threshold-based). Directional ramp favored for quick delta reading but has edge cases near neutral values.

2026-03-06 — Decision: use a directional ramp with an explicit neutral stop and an accent-emphasis token to indicate outliers. Trade-off documented: threshold bins reduce color confusion but increase cognitive steps for users examining continuous deltas.

2026-03-08 — Prototype: interactive Figma prototype uploaded showing hover/tooltips and keyboard focus states. Prototype includes density toggles; initial performance simulated by toggling 200-row table view.

2026-03-09 — Design review (UX): feedback from Lina (PM) — tooltip content should include absolute and relative values and a compact sparkline thumbnail. Action: add small caption lines and copy variations for admin vs end-user views.

2026-03-10 — Engineering review: Diego cautioned about using 8 distinct color stops for the ramp. Suggested 5 stops and building micro-gradients in canvas for continuous values. Action: create a mapping strategy (5-stop tokens + linear interpolation guidance).

2026-03-11 — Accessibility check: ran colorblind simulation; adjusted mid-tone contrast to meet 3:1 for UI indicators. High-contrast variants added. Request from Security to avoid embedding sensitive cost numbers in tooltip data attributes — use secure data fetch pattern.

2026-03-12 — Pre-handoff: prepared component spec and token table. Requesting design system review and backend contract: ENG to confirm payload shape for tooltip (absolute, relative, percentile, sampleTimestamp).
2026-03-12 — Next steps: finalize token names, add unit tests for visual regression snapshots, and open PR with CSS token mappings. Plan to merge and ship behind a feature flag for console-2026.04.
QA notes: ensure tooltip appears within viewport on narrow panels and keyboard focus order includes tooltip trigger elements.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens: add five new color-stop tokens and two high-contrast overrides; names follow DS naming convention (token names included in handoff CSV).
Components: tooltip component implemented with hover and keyboard focus, showing absolute + relative metrics and a 32x10 sparkline thumbnail.
Density: same component must adapt to compact/default/expanded density tokens without layout regression.
Accessibility: tooltip content and indicator states meet WCAG AA for normal text and 3:1 for UI indicators; keyboard-only users can open and dismiss tooltips.
Perf: rendered table with 500 rows of sparklines keeps time-to-first-paint within baseline budget (< 350ms on target infra).
Docs: include usage examples in the console design system page and sample GraphQL/REST payload contract for tooltip data.
Feature flag: shipped behind feature flag 'ds.tooltips.variance.v1' with telemetry events instrumented for rollout.
Cross-team signoff: design review approved, ENG feasibility confirmed, PM acceptance for rollout plan.
